{"analysis":"Yes. Assessing reusable components and the checkout integration boundary depends on which implementation target is established. The supplied decision_uncertainty explicitly leaves that target unconfirmed; absence at d5ddaa23ed61d3f62c1006584c18e612bacfdb64 does not establish absence in the intended target.

Keep only target resolution in this atom: establish the repository, branch or worktree, and exact revision intended for delivering Taggable’s agreed automatic 50% discount, using an authoritative existing record or, if none resolves it, the owner’s target decision. Done when that target and its authority are recorded unambiguously. If authority remains missing, report the specific missing decision and stop; target resolution is not complete.

Defer reusable-product-baseline assessment to the next atom. Against the resolved target, reconcile historical prerequisite, eligibility, recognition/payment evidence and selector contributions, check equivalent implementations, and identify the checkout entry point and pre-payment discount interface. Done when each capability has an evidence-linked source/test location or a bounded unresolved availability finding, historical proofs are distinguished from current compatibility, and the findings support a concrete next implementation scope or identify the exact remaining blocker. Restoration, adaptation and checkout integration remain subsequent work selected from those findings.

This narrows the recommendation to decision-enabling progress toward the discount delivery goal. No proposed work was executed."}
